content.text: Clag (also known as Nominations) is a British card game that originated in the Royal Air Force during World War II. The name is an acronym for 'Clouds Low Aircraft Grounded'â€”reflecting when air crews played while waiting for suitable weather. It combines Oh Hell!-style exact bidding with 22 deals including 8 special deals with unique rules (No Trumps, Misere, Blind, Twos Wild, etc.).

Clag originated in the British Royal Air Force during World War II. According to Taylor Foss, the name CLAG is an acronym for 'Clouds Low Aircraft Grounded'â€”air crews played this game while waiting for weather conditions suitable for flying. Also known as 'Clagg' or 'Cleg'.
4-7 players. Deal and play are clockwise.
Standard deck, score pad for cumulative scoring.
22 deals total. Deals 1-7: 1-7 cards each. Deals 8-15: special deals, 7 cards each. Deals 16-22: 7-1 cards each. Trump determined by turning next card after deal (except special deals).

items.text: Dealer Choice Variant: Dealer chooses number of cards (3-7) and whether normal or special deal. Winner of each deal becomes next dealer.
Alternative Scoring: Some score 2 points per trick in successful bid (e.g., bid of 2 scores 14 instead of 12).
